tombstone: Mirror with Auspicious Animals Surrounded by Rings of Squares and Semicircles (半圓方枚環繞式瑞獸鏡), late 100s CE. China, Eastern Han dynasty (25–220 CE). Bronze; diameter: 11.8 cm (4 5/8 in.); overall: 0.8 cm (5/16 in.); rim: 0.4 cm (3/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Drs. Thomas and Martha Carter in Honor of Sherman E. Lee, 1995.324

inscriptions.inscription:
吾作明鏡，幽凍三商。伯牙作樂，
眾神風容。宜大富兮，有福安服。
曾年益壽，子孫番昌，其師命長。
inscriptions.inscription_translation:
I made this bright mirror 
By refining the three metals.
BoYa is making music; 
The multitude of gods display their forms.
[The mirror] is suitable 
for a man with great wealth and good fortune.
He [who has it] will add years to life.
His descendants will also prosper.
Even this master will enjoy longevity.
